name: sign-in
title: Sign in
purpose: The sign-in screen: the product's name, one sentence, the fields, one primary action and a quiet link for trouble signing in, in a reading-width column at the leading edge.
whenToUse: For the screen a signed-out reader meets before anything else in the app.
For any other single focused task that stands outside the app's navigation, such as setting a new password or accepting an invitation. Keep the same shape: a name, a sentence, the fields, one action.
whenNotToUse: To ask for the password again inside the app, before a sensitive action. Use a dialog.
To describe or promote the product. This screen has no hero, no feature list and no picture. That belongs on the product's site.
For creating an account in several steps. Use the multi-step form.
With the app header or the navigation around it. A signed-out reader has nowhere to go, so the screen shows neither.
accessibility: In an app the element with ds-sign-in is the main element, and it is the only landmark on the page. The column starts at the leading edge of the page and is never centred.
ds-sign-in__product is a p holding the product's name. The h1 after it reads Sign in, and one sentence under it says which account to use. There is no other copy.

The fields are in one form. The email input has type="email" and autocomplete="username". The password is the catalogue's password field, with autocomplete="current-password", so a password manager can fill both and the reader can show what they typed before sending it. Neither uses a placeholder as its label.
Sign in is the form's submit button and the screen's one primary action. The link for trouble signing in is a quiet link after the form, and it names what it does.

When the sign-in is refused, keep the email, clear the password, and add an alert with role="alert" as the first thing in the form. Its title says what happened and its body says what to do. Link it from both inputs with aria-describedby, and move focus to the password input. Do not say which field was wrong.
While the form is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the button, change its label to Signing in, make the inputs read-only, set disabled on the password field's Show button and ignore further presses.
Tab moves through Email, Password, the Show button, Sign in, then the help link. Enter in either input sends the form. The pattern needs no script of its own.
